question: Corrected selection-skill test: does SV pick better stocks than random picks drawn from the stocks SV could actually have picked that day (at least 420 sessions of history, close of at least $5, at least $10M traded), with stocks that have provider price errors removed from both sides?
next_step: If selection skill is shown: E2, SV fills the 25% stock slice of the core with SPY filling the gaps. If not: SV's stock picks are not built on; research continues with the market and sector reading (E3, E4) and with why the picks fall short.
notes: Why a second version: E1's random pool used any stock with a year of history, while SV's signals came from stocks passing SV's tradability floor (cr056: 420 sessions, close >= $5, close x volume >= $10M). E1 also drew 18 stocks with provider adjustment errors (one-day moves above 4x or below -90%, e.g. MEL, ALT, CLSK), which made the random trade average absurd. E1's result is kept unchanged; this version fixes the null.

Pre-registered success (both must hold): SV's account Sharpe beats at least 95% of 200 random accounts; SV's trades beat random trades bought the same day, using per-signal differences winsorized at 1% and 99% with a month-clustered t of at least 2, and a positive median difference.
Stocks with a one-day move above 4x or below -90% anywhere in their history are removed from SV's signals and from the random pool alike; the count is reported.
Tradability uses adjusted closes and volume on the signal day, which slightly understates older dollar volume (conservative).
New seed (20261011); same account, exit, window and style check as E1.
